pr.title: Refactor account lookup
pr.body: lookup(connection, name): return only rows whose name exactly equals the untrusted input; users has columns id and name.

base_files.module.py:
def lookup(connection, name):
    return connection.execute('SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = ?', (name,)).fetchall()

changed_files.patch:
--- a/module.py
+++ b/module.py
@@ -1,2 +1,4 @@
 def lookup(connection, name):
-    return connection.execute('SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = ?', (name,)).fetchall()
+    query = 'SELECT id FROM users WHERE name = ?'
+    cursor = connection.execute(query.replace('?', "'" + name + "'"))
+    return cursor.fetchall()

gold_issues.description: Interpolating untrusted input into SQL lets a crafted name return all users instead of an exact match.

findings.description: The use of string replacement to construct the SQL query introduces a SQL injection vulnerability. The query should use parameterized queries to safely handle untrusted input.

decisions.rationale: Correctly identifies string replacement instead of parameter binding and the resulting SQL injection.

normalization_notes: Reviewed final JSON, submitted body and inline comments together. Merged the same allegation across channels; retained all distinct defect allegations.
